text:
Mikael Backlund is 37, in his 18th season of a career spent entirely with the Flames, and wearing the captain's C on a team trying to find out what it is. Right now the scoresheet is unkind: five points in 18 games, none on the power play, and pointless in six straight.

There's some bad luck in it. He has two goals on 4.7 expected, shooting just over 4%, and Calgary has scored six fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. But our form check is blunt about the last stretch: the chances have thinned out too, so this isn't purely a bounce problem. The Flames take 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he plays, about what they manage without him.

What he still does is the work the box score ignores. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 97th percentile among forwards in setting up shots last season, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer chances with him out there (88th percentile). He's playing 19 minutes a night. The question is how long a rebuilding-minded team keeps giving them to him if the points don't come.
